papers.title: Metal Additive Manufacturing For Lightweight Aerospace Structural Components
papers.abstract: Metal additive manufacturing (AM) is transforming aerospace engineering by enabling the fabrication of geometrically complex, lightweight structural components that are impossible to produce through conventional manufacturing. This paper investigates the mechanical performance of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) processed aerospace alloys—Ti-6Al-4V, Inconel 718, and AlSi10Mg—focusing on tensile properties, fatigue behavior, and the influence of post-processing treatments. Topology-optimized bracket designs achieved weight reductions of 52-75% while maintaining structural integrity under flight loads. LPBF specimens subjected to hot isostatic pressing (HIP) exhibited ultimate tensile strengths exceeding wrought equivalents by 8-14% and fatigue lives comparable to or exceeding conventional materials. Process-structure-property relationships were established through comprehensive microstructural characterization using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), micro-computed tomography (µ-CT), and fractography. The results validate LPBF as a viable production route for flight-critical aerospace components, provided appropriate post-processing and quality assurance protocols are implemented.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了Ti-6Al-4V的热等静压后处理对疲劳和力学性能的影响，与研究方向直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: Paper covers multiple alloys and is not exclusively focused on Ti-6Al-4V post-processing control; its primary scope is aerospace lightweight design.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索增材制造轻量化航空结构件的可行性。
summary_zh.method: 采用激光粉末床熔融制备三种合金，进行热等静压后处理并测试力学性能。
summary_zh.result: 热等静压后Ti-6Al-4V抗拉强度超过锻件8-14%，疲劳寿命与传统材料相当。
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观表征和力学测试验证工艺-结构-性能关系。

summary_en.motivation: This work aims to validate additive manufacturing for lightweight aerospace components by assessing mechanical performance of LPBF alloys with post-processing.
summary_en.method: Laser powder bed fusion was used to fabricate Ti-6Al-4V, Inconel 718, and AlSi10Mg, followed by hot isostatic pressing (HIP) and mechanical testing including tensile and fatigue.
summary_en.result: HIP-treated Ti-6Al-4V exhibited ultimate tensile strengths 8-14% higher than wrought counterparts and fatigue lives comparable to conventional materials.
summary_en.validation: Validation relied on microstructural characterization (EBSD, µ-CT, fractography) and mechanical testing of LPBF specimens with post-processing.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the viability of metal additive manufacturing for lightweight aerospace structural components.
summary_en.method: Mechanical performance of LPBF-processed aerospace alloys including Ti-6Al-4V was evaluated, focusing on tensile properties, fatigue behavior, and the influence of post-processing (HIP).
summary_en.result: HIP-treated specimens showed ultimate tensile strengths 8-14% higher than wrought equivalents and comparable or superior fatigue lives.
summary_en.validation: Validation through tensile and fatigue testing, along with microstructural characterization using EBSD, µ-CT, and fractography.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的压痕测试验证方法，直接相关于力学与疲劳性能评估。
llm.why_not_core: No fatigue or tensile testing results; focuses on indentation-based build verification rather than direct mechanical property characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用压痕测试方法验证增材制造Ti-6Al-4V构件的质量。
summary_zh.method: 采用压痕测试技术对打印件进行力学性能评估。
summary_zh.result: 证明了压痕测试可作为有效的构件验证手段。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验压痕测试数据验证方法有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To develop indentation test methods for verifying the build quality of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V components.
summary_en.method: Indentation testing was applied to assess mechanical properties such as hardness and modulus.
summary_en.result: Indentation proved effective for rapid build verification of Ti-6Al-4V parts.
summary_en.validation: Experimental indentation measurements validated the approach against known mechanical properties.
